text:
Early-season run-scoring has not been a problem for the Silver Spring-Takoma Thunderbolts, a positive turnaround from last year. But the pitching staff has struggled so far, as the team has a 1-4 record heading into a week with three home games.

The TBolts will be hosting the Alexandria Aces, Bethesda Big Train, and Metro South County Braves on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday of this week. Each game begins at 7 p.m. at Blair High School Field.

After a heartbreaking ninth-inning, 12-11 loss at the Big Train on Opening Night, the Thunderbolts were flat against the Gaithersburg Giants and Olney Cropdusters in their first two home games. They lost those contests 20-8 and 25-1, as both pitchers and fielders looked out of sync from layoffs of a few weeks after collegiate seasons ended for many of them.

The team rebounded with a 13-5 win over the DC Grays before dropping a game to the Big Train, 27-13, on Sunday night.

Heading into the season, Coach Brock Hunter said that he felt the TBolts would put up runs more consistently than a year ago. “We have players who I think will hit for average,” he said. After five games, that has been the case, as their batting average is a superb .286 and the team is tied for third in runs scored.

On the mound, however, Hunter warned, “To win consistently, you’ve got to be able to throw strikes.” So far that has been a lesson learned the hard way, as the Tbolts staff has issued the most walks in the league by a wide margin and has the worst ERA.

Pitching Coach Ryan Mariani observed that the team has a good mixture of returning players and new faces. “We have some big arms in the bullpen, and we’re working early in the season on figuring out our starters,” he said.

The best start so far was by Jacob Seek (Chesapeake College), who gave up 1 run in 3 innings against Gaithersburg. Braden Fetheroff (Clarion Univ.) and Brady Grimes (Millersville Univ.) have also been tapped as starters.

One intriguing reliever is Josh Erd, who played third base the last two seasons for the Thunderbolts. Erd became a relief pitcher this season at East Stroudsburg University and is seeking to improve his mechanics and raise his velocity into the mid-90s this summer. “I never pitched, but my coaches always knew I had a strong arm,” Erd said. “It’s great working on something completely new and different in my baseball life.”

As the second week of the season arrives, Hunter reminds his players that effort and consistency are keys to winning. “Every year I emphasize a few basic things to the guys: be a good teammate, play hard, play with confidence,” he said.

For the full Thunderbolts schedule and information about games and summer camps, go to Tbolts.org.
